at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (24.11.2026) In order to accelerate permit-granting procedures for renewable energy projects, the revised Renewable Energy Directive (RED)1 introduced a rebuttable presumption that renewable energy projects are of overriding public interest2. However, the provisions on derogations in the Birds3 and Habitats4 Directives remain fully applicable and, where relevant, national authorities must assess if the cumulative conditions to benefit from the derogations are met. Both interests are thus carefully balanced. Another relevant aspect of the revised RED is that Member States may designate renewables acceleration areas for wind energy projects. Such strategic planning allows to select areas with the lowest environmental impacts5. The Commission does not have figures on the number of wind farms that were granted a derogation as regards protected species. In March 2026 the Commission adopted a guidance document on the species protection provisions under the Birds Directive6. This document provides practical advice to Member States and stakeholders in implementing the existing rules and the related European Court of Justice case-law. The guidance also has a section that clarifies how the species protection provisions can be applied correctly with regards to certain economic activities, including wind energy development and operation as well as providing some established mitigation measures. Tackling climate change through renewable energy deployment contributes to reducing biodiversity loss7. Wind energy deployment and biodiversity protection and enhancement can go hand in hand through appropriate siting, planning and management8.
1 Directive (EU) 2018/2001 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 December 2018 on the

promotion of the use of energy from renewable sources (OJ L 328, 21.12.2018, p. 82), as amended by Directive (EU) 2023/2413 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 18 October 2023 (OJ L, 2023/2413, 31.10.2023). 2 See Art. 16f of the Renewable Energy Directive. 3 Directive 2009/147/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 30 November 2009 on the conservation of wild birds, OJ L 20, 26.1.2010, pp. 7–25. 4 Council Directive 92/43/EEC of 21 May 1992 on the conservation of natural habitats and of wild fauna and flora, OJ L 206, 22.7.1992, pp. 7–50. 5 See Art. 15c (1) a) of the Renewable Energy Directive. 6 https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/C/2026/4094/oj/eng. 7 Climate change is a major and growing driver of biodiversity loss, see for instance Henrique M. Pereira et al., Global trends and scenarios for terrestrial biodiversity and ecosystem services from 1900 to 2050, Science 384,458-465(2024), DOI: https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.adn3441. 8 See for instance https://www.birdlife.org/news/2026/05/06/from-conflict-to-coexistence-protecting-birds-andbiodiversity-from-wind-energy/.
